newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MADRID-BETIS DRAW MAY LET BARCELONA BACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MADRID-BETIS DRAW MAY LET BARCELONA BACK.

text.p: Saturday's top-of-the-table clash between Real Madrid and Real Betis lived up to the highest expectations and was undoubtedly one of the most memorable games played in Spain this season.
But the 2-2 draw may be best remembered for letting a third team, Barcelona, back into the championship race.
Second-placed Barcelona beat Racing Santander to narrow Real Madrid's lead to six points and put four points between themselves and Betis.
However, while Barcelona were once again disappointing fans with unimaginative play, Real Madrid and Betis delighted a huge nationwide television audience.
"A gift from the gods" read a headline in the sports daily 'As', "Madrid and Betis offered an intense clash that had everything."
One player stood out above all the others in the post-match analysis.

Commentators who had centred attention on Alfonso Perez were not disappointed by the Betis striker, who scored against his old club with an early header and stretched goalkeeper Bodo Illgner with several other efforts.
Alfonso, who netted twice in last week's World Cup win over Malta, completely outshone another product of the Real Madrid junior team system, teenager Raul Gonzalez.
"Right now we can't do without Alfonso," Betis manager Serra Ferrer said.

But Madrid manager Fabio Capello, former coach of AC Milan, had harsh words for the striker, particularly in connection with an incident which resulted in a booking for central defender Fernando Hierro.
"Alfonso is a great player but he's a player who throws himself a lot. He wasn't even touched...We're going to appeal against the card (booking)," Capello said.
Capello said he had not seen a separate incident just before halftime in which Alfonso was wrestled to the ground by Hierro on the edge of the penalty area.
The majority of retired referees now working for the media agreed that a penalty should have been given.
Before the game Capello had hit out at the Spanish Federation's appeal court for quashing a yellow card which would have meant the automatic suspension of Alfonso for Saturday's match.
"A card...should be something you can't appeal against," Capello said.
His feelings found sympathy with several figures in the Spanish game who fear that refereeing decisions may end up in the country's notoriously slow legal system.
But for Betis fans, who gleefully welcomed their team back from Madrid, nothing was going to spoil their big day.
With a game in hand Betis are now five points clear of their nearest challengers for a UEFA Cup place and may yet push Barcelona for Spain's second European Cup place.
The current success has been awaited with patient devotion by the long-suffering Betis faithful.
"Being a Betis fan is a sentiment that is a bit like a religion," coach Ferrer said.
